mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's recent-5 shots FOR exceeds its all-prior shots FOR by a meaningful margin AND its recent-5 shots AGAINST is substantially below its all-prior shots AGAINST. Within that joint regime, measure Team B's corner_kicks FOR versus Team A's corner_kicks AGAINST (recent-5 vs all-prior).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team simultaneously shows elevated shots FOR and suppressed shots AGAINST in recent matches, its corner-kick production rises relative to its long-run average, while the opponent's corner-kick production is suppressed relative to their long-run average.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-volume surge in recent matches (shots FOR) co-occurs with a simultaneous collapse in shots conceded (shots AGAINST), suggesting a joint offensive-defensive momentum regime that is structurally different from either observable measured alone. The relationship to test is whether matches where a team simultaneously shows rising shots FOR and falling shots AGAINST produce a different corner-kick differential than the long-run baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint intersection of two distinct observables (shots FOR trend AND shots AGAINST trend) for the same team simultaneously, which cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. Neither shots FOR alone nor shots AGAINST alone captures the combined regime.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where one side's recent shots_on_target FOR is elevated above its all-prior level while the opposing side's recent shots_on_target FOR is below its all-prior level. Within that asymmetric shot-quality regime, measure the second-half card total (cards_2h) for the defensively pressured side against the competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one side holds a strong recent advantage in shots_on_target relative to the opponent's recent level, the defensively pressured side's second-half cards rise above the competition-context baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots_on_target FOR has surged in recent matches while Team A's shots_on_target FOR has declined in recent matches. The joint asymmetry across the two sides' shot quality (on-target rate) may condition the second-half card environment differently from what either team's card rate alone would predict, because a dominant attacking side tends to draw more defensive fouls and cards in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism involves an asymmetric cross-team comparison of the same observable (shots_on_target FOR for Team B vs. shots_on_target FOR for Team A in recent form) jointly conditioning a different observable (cards_2h). It is not reducible to one team's shots_on_target alone or one team's cards_2h alone.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where both the home team's fouls FOR (recent) and the away team's fouls AGAINST (recent) are simultaneously above their respective all-prior averages. Within that joint high-foul-pressure regime, measure yellow_cards FOR for the home team against the competition baseline for yellow cards.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both a team's own recent foul rate and its opponent's recent foul-suffering rate are simultaneously elevated above their long-run averages, yellow cards for the fouling team rise above the competition-context yellow-card baseline in a manner that exceeds what either foul rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent fouls FOR have risen sharply above both its all-prior level and the competition baseline, while Team B's recent fouls AGAINST have also risen. The joint elevation of Team A's foul-committing rate and Team B's foul-suffering rate creates a compound disciplinary pressure that may non-linearly amplify yellow-card production beyond what either team's individual foul rate would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint intersection of two distinct observables (fouls FOR for Team A AND fouls AGAINST for Team B) simultaneously elevated, then related to a third observable (yellow_cards). This is not reducible to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the home team's home goals FOR average exceeds its away goals FOR average by a meaningful margin AND the away team's away goals AGAINST average exceeds its home goals AGAINST average by a meaningful margin. Within that joint home-advantage / away-vulnerability intersection, measure total goals against the competition-context goals baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team has a strong home scoring advantage and the away team has a pronounced away defensive vulnerability simultaneously, total goals in the match rise above the competition-context baseline in a manner not captured by either team's split alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A shows a pronounced home-vs-away split in goals FOR (home substantially higher than away) while Team B shows a pronounced home-vs-away split in goals FOR (home substantially higher than away) and goals AGAINST (away substantially higher than home). The joint interaction of Team A's home goal-scoring advantage and Team B's away defensive vulnerability — both measured simultaneously — may condition total goals in a way that neither team's home/away split alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires the simultaneous joint conditioning on two distinct venue-split dimensions — one for Team A (home goals FOR vs away goals FOR) and one for Team B (away goals AGAINST vs home goals AGAINST) — which is a two-opponent-descriptor interaction not reducible to a single observable with one venue band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the home team's first-half goals FOR average exceeds its second-half goals FOR average AND the away team's second-half goals AGAINST average exceeds its first-half goals AGAINST average. Within that joint timing-asymmetry regime, measure first-half goals FOR for the home team and second-half goals AGAINST for the away team against their respective competition-context baselines.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team has a historically front-loaded goal-scoring profile and the away team has a historically back-loaded goal-conceding profile simultaneously, first-half goals in the match are elevated relative to the competition baseline, while the second half also remains elevated — producing a flatter within-match goal distribution than the competition norm.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are distributed with a higher share in the first half than the second half (first-half goals FOR above second-half goals FOR), while Team B's goals AGAINST are distributed with a higher share in the second half than the first half (second-half goals AGAINST above first-half goals AGAINST). This cross-team, cross-half asymmetry in goal-timing profiles — where one team scores early and the other concedes late — may condition the half-level goal distribution differently from what either team's half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This mechanism requires jointly conditioning on two distinct half-level splits across two different teams and two different perspectives (home team's goals FOR by half vs. away team's goals AGAINST by half), which is a within-match state dependence combined with a cross-team asymmetry. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.
